title: We have reached the evening
cue: "We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah…"
arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرِ مَا فِيهَا، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهَا، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَالْهَرَمِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ وَفِتْنَةِ الدُّنْيَا وَعَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ
transliteration: Amsaynaa wa'amsal-mulku lillaah, wal-hamdu lillaah, laa ilaha illallaahu wahdahu laa shareeka lah, allaahumma innee as'aluka min khayri hadhihil-laylati wakhayri maa feehaa, wa'a'oodhu bika min sharrihaa washarri maa feehaa, allaahumma innee a'oodhu bika minal-kasali wal-harami wasoo'il-kibari wafitnatid-dunyaa wa'adhaabil-qabr
translation: We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge with You from its evil and the evil of what is in it. O Allah, I seek refuge with You from laziness, from decrepitude, from the evil of old age, from the trials of this world and from the punishment of the grave.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sahih Muslim, ed. Muhammad Fu’ad Abd al-Baqi, hadith 2723: https://shamela.ws/book/1727/6841

when: Evening; in the morning with its opening changed
usage.evidence: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reports that the Prophet ﷺ said this in the evening (Muslim 2723, the narration of Za'idah). Another narration under the same number adds, after "without partner", His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things; and says that in the morning he opened with "We have reached the morning".

variants.label: In the morning he said the same, opening with these words.
